lines.text: You opened a connection. You proved it is safe. Now what? You ask for the page.
Your browser builds an HTTP request. Method, path, headers. A plain-text letter to the server.
It travels over your encrypted TLS tunnel. One packet at a time, across the internet.
The server receives it. Reads the route. Finds the handler. Starts working.
The application runs. Queries a database. Computes a response. Builds HTML or JSON.
The response comes back. Status line. 200 OK. Headers. Body. Encrypted, sent back.
Packets flow back across the same path. Your browser receives them, in order, thanks to TCP.
Your browser parses the HTML. Builds the DOM. Fetches CSS, images, JavaScript.
Remember the two hundred milliseconds? DNS, TCP, TLS, HTTP. They all fit inside it.
Next: how those bytes reach millions of users at once. CDNs and the edge.
